experiment: HD1.1 NIST ASD alkali-ns controlled hypothesis-discovery pilot
purpose: Validate the auditable hypothesis lifecycle on real measurements before attempting novel open-ended discovery.
scientific_novelty_boundary: Rydberg-series structure is established physics. Recovering it validates system behavior, not discovery of a new scientific law.

source.name: NIST Atomic Spectra Database
source.excluded: all NIST parenthesized theoretical, bracketed semi-empirical, and question-marked rows

data_roles.unit: spectrum-specific ns Rydberg series sorted by principal quantum number n
data_roles.discovery: lowest 70 percent of n values, with at least six rows
data_roles.heldout_falsification: highest remaining 30 percent of n values, with at least two rows

selection.validation: rolling-origin one-step-ahead extrapolation within each discovery series
selection.score: mean across six spectra of median absolute prediction error divided by discovery energy range, plus 0.005 per fitted parameter

fitting.loss: deterministic unweighted soft-L1 nonlinear least squares
fitting.reason_unweighted: NIST measurement uncertainty is far smaller than expected model discrepancy and must not dominate structural selection

claim_boundary: HD1.1 is a controlled calibration pilot on known alkali-series physics. It cannot support a claim of novel scientific discovery or general hypothesis-discovery superiority. Any future confirmation must use untouched orbital/transition families and a separately frozen contract.
